title: One command name, many branches

blocks.md:
## `switch` routes a command

A dispatch table reads one value and picks a branch. `switch (cmd)` compares with `===`, runs the matching `case`, and keeps running **into the next case** until it meets `break`.

That fall-through is a feature when you group spellings:

```
case "east":
case "e":
  Player.move("east")
  break
```

Both labels share one body. Forgetting `break` on a branch that has its own body is the classic bug: the fox does two things for one command. `default` catches anything you did not plan for.

blocks.promptMd: A `case "east"` moves east but has no `break`. The next case moves south. What happens on `"east"`?

choices.md: East runs, then south runs too

blocks.promptMd: The plan contains `"beep"`, which no case names. With a `default` branch that calls `Player.say("skip")`, what happens?

choices.md: The program throws on the unknown command
The default branch runs and the fox says `skip`

blocks.explainMd: `default` is the branch for everything you did not list. Without it, an unknown command is silently ignored.

blocks.promptMd: > Walk the plan with a `switch`. `east` and `e` both go east, `south` goes south, and anything else falls to `default` and says `skip`. Beacon is at (2, 2).

hintLadder.md: The plan is already in the file. Loop it and branch on each command.
`switch (cmd)` with one `case` per command name, and `break` at the end of each body.
Two labels stacked with no body between them share the branch below: `case "east":` then `case "e":` then the move.

const plan = ["east", "east", "south", "south", "beep"]
for (const cmd of plan) {
  switch (cmd) {
    case "east":
    case "e":
      Player.move("east")
      break
    case "south":
      Player.move("south")
      break
    default:
      Player.say("skip")
  }
}

description: One command name picks between many branches. Grouped labels share a body on purpose, and a missing stop runs the next branch by accident.
